sections.title: Profile
sections.text:
A member of Reserve Op Team A6. At her own request, she has been reclassified as a Guard Operator, and has shown a formidable talent for close-quarters fighting and for handling heavy melee weapons. Beyond A6's routine duties, she also frequently takes part, in a personal capacity, in field assignments that require venturing into dangerous territory.
Everyone says that the Catapult who used to love slacking off and cutting corners has changed completely. To that assessment, she offers neither agreement nor denial.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 5%
Operator Catapult displays clear symptoms of Oripathy.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.33u/L
Owing to her frequent forays into high-risk environments and her participation in high-intensity combat, Operator Catapult's condition carries a risk of deterioration.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
Orchid and Catapult each submitted their own version of the mission report on the trip to the Bubbly Realm. Orchid's was as meticulous as ever, laying out the whole course of events with perfect clarity; Catapult's left the reader not knowing whether to laugh or cry—
She turned in a report that was, by her own reckoning, extremely detailed—except that its contents concerned nothing but hunting.
Indeed, from Catapult's mission report alone you could never work out what she and Orchid actually went through in the Bubbly Realm. What you will know by the end of it, without fail, is what the country around the Bubbly Realm is like, what sort of monsters live there, and whether those monsters are edible.
Even Orchid was taken aback when she read it, wondering when on earth Catapult had gathered all of this. Catapult, looking thoroughly proud of herself, ran through it for her point by point: which monster the ingredients of such-and-such a dish they ate in the Bubbly Realm had actually come from, which monster that meat they ate by the campfire that one time had come from, and so on—adding that Orchid had simply been too busy scowling all day to pay attention to any of it.
It has to be said: as a mission report, Catapult's document is unquestionably worth zero marks—but as a gazetteer of the local land and its wildlife, it deserves full marks.
What's more, the pair's adventure was so outlandish that no matter how exhaustively Orchid wrote it up, doubts were inevitable—and Catapult's report dispelled them nicely. Anyone with a silver tongue can make up a story; making up an entire ecosystem, however, is well beyond the ordinary person.

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
When we get together, we often play competitive board games.
Who wins always follows a pattern—while everyone is still unfamiliar with the rules, Catapult tends to win the most; once everyone has more or less figured the rules out, it is Spot or me who wins.
And the more Catapult wins early on, the more miserably she loses later. Partly this is because she is very good at using the rules to obstruct everyone else on her way to victory; her wins are invariably built on the suffering of one person, or several, so retaliation usually follows—sometimes from outside the game, as when I assign her a little extra work. Partly it is because, once the novelty of the opening wears off, she visibly loses interest in the game and merely goes through the motions for the rest of it.
This lines up perfectly with the impression she gives: enthusiasm that lasts three minutes, and an unwillingness to spend much time on anything. Such a temperament is hardly rare—put another way, it is a trait a great many children going through adolescence share: brimming with energy, yet with no idea where to pour that passion.
With age and experience, most children either lose that energy or find something to pour their passion into. What makes Catapult unusual is that even at her age she still holds on to both the energy and the frustration of having no fixed goal... All right, I don't actually think that is so unusual. If anything, the adults who fancy themselves mature have, more often than not, merely lost the appetite for searching and picked something at random to call their goal.
As one of those adults, most of the time I dislike this childish streak of hers. Just as with our board games, there is so much you can plainly tell she could do better, and she simply won't—and it lands extra trouble on my desk more often than not.
You could say the only effect time and experience have had on her is that she now knows exactly how much responsibility she has to bear for what she does. When she wants to squeeze some fun out of something that has already bored her, she knows precisely which kinds of trouble are manageable—the kind that ends with me chewing her out—and that makes her look all the more 'insufferable' much of the time. But, well, what am I supposed to do about it?
I bring all this up because I want to set one thing straight—since we came back from Sargon, quite a few colleagues have felt that Catapult has changed. From where I stand, she has not changed in the slightest.
Thank goodness. If that inexplicable trip to the Bubbly Realm contributed anything at all to Rhodes Island, I suspect it is this one thing: Catapult has finally found a toy she cannot put down—and by the look of it, she will not be losing her enthusiasm for it for a very long time.
—From 'Supplementary Records on the Bubbly Realm Incident'

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
In the reclassification assessment on Catapult submitted to the Doctor, Dobermann made a point of noting Catapult's attitude toward combat. It reads as follows:
I have met many warriors who love fighting for its own sake, and there are no few of them on Rhodes Island. Their attitude toward combat generally comes down to this: 'I want to prove through battle that I am growing stronger. I am fighting myself; I want to keep surpassing myself.' For them, combat is a trial.
At first, hearing others talk about Catapult's situation, I assumed her personality had changed, and found it odd—it did not sound like her.
After the assessment I understood at once. Her attitude... I have seen it before in certain people. What that sort pursues is not simply becoming stronger, but the thrill of life and death separated by a hair's breadth. Catapult is the same. She has no notion of testing her own limits or holding a dialogue with herself; she simply finds fighting giant monsters thrilling enough to stave off the boredom inside her.
Put that way, I can actually understand why she made this shift.
What the two types have in common is that both grow strong quickly. The difference is that people like Catapult tend not to live long.
The Palico called Masamune seems to think highly of that hunter's quality in her, and I can see why. In the context of nature there is indeed nothing wrong with it—failing again and again, challenging again and again, growing stronger again and again, they themselves become a link in the law of the jungle.
Of course, I understand your concern as well, Doctor. For people like this, all training is merely a means of chasing a stronger thrill, and the consequence of chasing that thrill without limit is inevitably ruinous.
That said, I do not think you need to worry too much.
Compared with her own 'kind,' Catapult differs in a few respects.
If I had to sum it up, I would say: she is not pure. Catapult will never be able to throw everything she has into the hunt.
And the reason for that is obvious, is it not?

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
Catapult quickly made a name for herself in certain explorer and hunter circles, and a number of professional teams held out offers to her—all of which she turned down.
She has given the question some thought, because big sis Orchid is forever telling every member of Squad A6, in that patient, well-meaning way of hers, that they should not think only of the present and ought to spare a thought for the future.
Clearly, this is exactly the sort of question big sis Orchid wants her to think about.
Once in a while—usually when she is bored out of her mind—she does ask herself: what do you want to do with your future?
Even more rarely, to answer the expectant look in big sis Orchid's eyes, she has tried hard to come up with an answer—only to find that she genuinely cannot.
It seems she will never become the sort of person who prepares for the future the way big sis Orchid does.
But she does not think she counts as someone who savors the present either—after all, that sort of person would not be as slack as she is.
She skips training, treats her assignments with a casual shrug, and beyond Squad A6 has no particular interest in keeping up relationships.
Big sis Orchid is always scolding her for drifting through life in a daze, and she thinks of herself the same way. But in truth she knows: she simply does not see what the point of any of it is.
Dimly, she feels that she is waiting—waiting for something to appear that she can truly throw her energy into.
When she tells big sis Orchid this conclusion, Orchid says, 'If you never try anything, you will never find what suits you.'
Now, she feels she may have found it. She likes hunting, so joining a team dedicated to hunting would seem the better choice, and she would bet that big sis Orchid would back the idea—on the surface, at least.
But she is not as contrary as big sis Orchid. Orchid will not admit that she loves Squad A6; she is nothing like that.
She has never once denied that she loves every member of Squad A6—their personalities, and that one-of-a-kind space that comes into being only when they are together.
Give that up? She would sooner give up hunting.
That is right—so what troubles her is not whether she should leave Squad A6 for the sake of what she is after, but how to talk the rest of A6 into joining her hunting venture. Cannot talk them into it? Then drag them along!
She already has a few ideas. She can trick—no, persuade—Spot into drawing a hunting manga with her: she writes the script, Spot draws, and then a cracking plot reels Popukar in and gets her hooked on hunting too. Midnight is a bit of a problem—oh, right, she has collected so many of his business cards that putting him to work at his actual job is hardly out of the question. As for big sis Orchid, well, if everyone else is coming, of course Orchid will come too!
That is settled, then!
She thinks smugly: one day she is going to hunt the mightiest beast on this land! And by then, Squad A6 will surely be the mightiest squad on this land too! Probably!

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
The weapon manual Masamune brought along introduces the techniques of every hunting weapon in detail. By now, every blank space in the Charge Blade manual has been filled in completely with Catapult's notes.
Of course, calling them notes is generous—most of what is written there is not especially serious.
Beside 'Morphing Advance,' for instance, she has drawn a long row of tally marks, counting how many times she failed to morph in time and slammed into a wall.
And above the move 'Counter Peak Performance' she has scrawled two lines in large letters—'Check your Wirebug before you use this! It only blocks ONE attack! Do not lean on it too much!'—along with a set of stick-figure sketches of herself getting flung through the air by a monster after getting carried away.
The material next to 'Axe Hopper' is even more exasperating. There is some thinking about combat technique—hit placement and the like—but far more of it is devoted to researching which pose looks coolest when she unleashes an Aerial Super Amped Element Discharge, and by the look of it she never did arrive at an answer.
Next to 'Condensed Spinning Slash,' however, she has written down some genuinely earnest thoughts of her own—
Focus everything on a single instant, block the opponent's strongest blow, then hit back with my strongest Super Amped Element Discharge. That big, sweeping feeling is the very essence of the Charge Blade.
This move is fun in its own right, though—you could say it changes the whole style of the Charge Blade. It does not lean on split-second guarding or heavy attacks; it is all about reacting on the spot, hunting for an opening while you dodge. And it handles just like Popukar's chainsaw. Such a shame I did not get to use it back in the Bubbly Realm.
I still prefer the former, but the Condensed Spinning Slash has its own kind of fun—ha, and the Axe Hopper is a blast too. This Charge Blade really is more interesting than I ever imagined!
